pr_summary: Add linux-aarch64 platform support to cancerit-allelecount recipe. The fix adds 'linux-aarch64' to the extra.additional-platforms list in meta.yaml, updates build number from 6 to 7, adds run_exports, improves license metadata, and modifies build.sh to use parallel make (-j ${CPU_COUNT}) and set -xeu for verbose error reporting.
patch_file_cues: meta.yaml: increments build number from 6 to 7
meta.yaml: improves license metadata (GPL-3.0-only, license_file, license_family)
build.sh: changes 'set -eu' to 'set -xeu' for verbose error output
build.sh: changes 'make' to 'make -j ${CPU_COUNT}' for parallel build
test_file_cues: meta.yaml test section contains: 'alleleCounter -h' command test
Test is a simple smoke test verifying binary execution
platform_constraint_evidence: README.md states bioconda supports 'Linux and macOS, supporting both x86_64 and aarch64/arm64 architectures'
azure-pipeline.yml runs on ubuntu-latest for Linux builds
fix.patch adds 'linux-aarch64' to additional-platforms, indicating cross-platform support
Recipe has 'skip: True # [osx]' indicating it builds on Linux
notes: Bioconda is a conda channel for bioinformatics packages. The repository uses bioconda-utils for building and testing recipes. The cancerit-allelecount recipe is a C-based tool that requires htslib, zlib, bzip2, and xz. The fix enables building on linux-aarch64 architecture by adding it to additional-platforms. The build system uses conda-build via bioconda-utils. Testing is done via mulled containers (Docker-based). The recipe currently skips macOS builds. The platform is fully compatible with Linux x86-64 containers for testing.
